response.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM orders AS o JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(tc.order_count) AS average_count_above_average, AVG(tc.order_count - overall.average_count) AS average_excess FROM type_counts AS tc CROSS JOIN overall WHERE tc.order_count > overall.average_count

assumptions.assumption: The average across types includes only order types with at least one matched order.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every order type present in orders, assigning zero to types with no matched orders.
alternatives.sql: WITH types AS (SELECT DISTINCT ordertune FROM orders), matched AS (SELECT DISTINCT o.orderspivot, o.ordertune FROM orders AS o JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault), type_counts AS (SELECT t.ordertune, COUNT(m.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM types AS t LEFT JOIN matched AS m ON m.ordertune IS t.ordertune GROUP BY t.ordertune), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(tc.order_count) AS average_count_above_average, AVG(tc.order_count - overall.average_count) AS average_excess FROM type_counts AS tc CROSS JOIN overall WHERE tc.order_count > overall.average_count
